Apple's FY2025 10-K says it applied a Monte Carlo value-at-risk (VAR) model to its foreign currency derivative positions. The model estimates, with 95% confidence, a maximum one-day loss in fair value of $590 million as of September 27, 2025. The comparable figure was $538 million as of September 28, 2024.
Apple applied a value-at-risk (VAR) model to its foreign currency derivative positions to assess the potential impact of fluctuations in exchange rates. The model used a Monte Carlo simulation.
Apple defines the VAR as the maximum expected loss in fair value, for a given confidence interval, to its foreign currency derivative positions due to adverse movements in rates.
Apple estimates, with 95% confidence, a maximum one-day loss in fair value of $590 million as of September 27, 2025. The comparable figure was $538 million as of September 28, 2024.
